threads.thread_goal: Align on current sorting workflow, main bottlenecks and safety pain points.

messages.text:
Kickoff for the mixed-waste sorting line upgrade.
Can everyone drop a quick rundown of how the line actually runs on your shift and where it hurts most?
I will start mapping the current workflow for T1 and sketching on the layout map in A6, but I need your view from each position.
Please call out:
- where material piles up
- where you see most contamination
- any spots that feel unsafe or cramped
We also need to agree later on the top three bottlenecks and which section we use as the pilot area.

On early shift, the first pile-up is right after the infeed belt where bags get dropped on the floor when the belt is full.
We also get a lot of glass mixed with plastics at the first manual pick station.
Safety-wise, the corner near the compactor feels tight when the forklift comes through.
For T1 I can help list the top pain points from early shift if that works.

From the recycling side, the biggest issue I see is mixed hazardous items ending up on the general line: paint tins with liquid still inside, small batteries, and aerosol cans.
They usually show up around the second manual pick station.
We also lose time when the hazardous cage is blocked by full pallets.
For the map in A6, I suggest we mark:
- infeed belt
- first pick station
- second pick station
- compactor corner
- hazardous cage and chemical drum area.
That will make it easier to pick a pilot section later.

On late shift we get a lot of bags stacked near the infeed because the forklift is dropping mixed loads faster than we can sort.
I also notice people stepping over hoses near the wash station, feels a bit risky when the floor is wet.
Not sure if that is part of T1 or another task, but it slows us down.

From my side, cleaning between shifts is hard because there is still material on the floor around the compactor and under the belt.
We often run out of time to do a proper sweep and check.
If we change the layout in A6, can we leave more space around the compactor so we can clean better?

Adding to what others said: when I am on forklift, the path past the hazardous cage and the compactor is the tightest.
Sometimes there are extra bins parked in the aisle.
That is where I see near misses with people walking through.
For T1 I can mark the forklift paths and pinch points on the map if someone prints A6 and leaves it at the line.

Thanks all, this is helpful.
Let me summarise what we have so far for T1:
- Bottleneck 1: infeed belt and floor pile-up before first pick station.
- Bottleneck 2: mixed hazardous items at second pick station and blocked access to hazardous cage.
- Bottleneck 3: tight forklift path and congestion around compactor and hazardous cage.
- Extra: cleaning time lost because of material left on floor and under belt.
Can you confirm if these feel like the main three, or are we missing something bigger?

From early shift, that list matches what we see.
If we fix the infeed and the compactor area, cleaning will also get easier.
I am ok with those as the main three.

Agree on those three.
The hazardous items at the second pick station are a big risk and slow us down.
If we treat that as part of bottleneck 2, I am aligned.
We can handle the detailed rules later in the hazardous guideline and SOP, but for T1 this is the right focus.

No other bigger issues from my side.
The forklift path and compactor corner are where I feel most pressure.
Happy to focus there as one of the three.

Same on late shift.
If we can stop the pile-up at the infeed and clear the compactor area, the line runs smoother.
I am fine with those three.

Ok, sounds like we have alignment.
For the record, the three bottlenecks we will tackle first are:
1) Infeed belt and floor pile-up before first pick station.
2) Mixed hazardous items and access to hazardous cage around second pick station.
3) Forklift congestion and tight space around compactor and hazardous cage.
I will mark these clearly on A6 as part of T1.

Next, we need to pick a pilot area where we try layout and routine changes first.
My suggestion is to use the stretch from the first pick station through to the compactor corner, including the hazardous cage access.
Reason: it covers all three bottlenecks and we can isolate it without stopping the whole line for more than short windows.
Any objections or better ideas?

That pilot stretch makes sense to me.
We can still feed the rest of the line while we test small changes there, as long as we coordinate with the shift supervisor for short pauses.
It also lets us test hazardous handling changes without touching the whole plant at once.

Works for early shift.
If we know in advance when we are trialling changes there, we can plan cleaning and checks around it.
No objections from me.

From forklift side, that is the area where layout changes will help most.
I am ok using that as the pilot.
We just need clear markings on the floor once we agree the new paths.

Fine by me.
If we can also test a better way to keep that area clean during the pilot, that would help a lot.

Thanks all.
Confirming: the pilot area will be from the first pick station through to the compactor corner, including access to the hazardous cage.
I will update A6 to highlight that zone and finish the T1 workflow map with these details.
Next threads will cover the SOP, layout and routines for that pilot stretch.

threads.thread_goal: Define and lock the standard sorting and contamination control procedure.

messages.text:
I have put together a first draft of the mixed-waste sorting SOP based on what we see on the line and the pilot area we picked.
This will become A1.
It covers:
- steps from infeed to compactor
- how to pull out contaminants
- what to do with hazardous items
This draft also links to a simple load check list that will become A2.
Can you all look at it with your shift in mind and comment on anything that is unclear or missing?
This work ties to T2 and T3.

Thanks for drafting this.
From a quick read, the flow matches what we mapped in T1.
One question: in the step where we remove sharp metal, can we be more explicit about which bin it goes to and how often it should be cleared?
That will help avoid overflow at the pilot area.

On early shift, the part about PPE is clear, but the step about double-checking for liquids in containers might slow us down.
Could we tie that to the checklist in A2 so we only do the extra check on loads that look risky, like when we see a lot of paint tins?

I got a bit lost in the part about aerosols.
It says to move them to the hazardous cage, but I am not sure which container exactly.
Can we add a simple line like: 'put aerosols in the blue drum near the cage door' or similar?

For cleaning between shifts, it would help if the SOP says when to stop feeding the belt so we can clear the line and do a quick contamination check before we start sweeping.
Right now people keep feeding while we try to clean.

Good points.
I will update A1 so that:
- sharp metal from the pilot area goes into the labelled scrap bin next to the second pick station, emptied at least once per shift by the forklift driver.
- aerosols go into the blue drum by the hazardous cage door, as suggested.
For the liquids check, I like the idea of tying it to A2.
We can add a checklist item: 'If load has many cans or containers, tap and tilt a sample to check for liquids before compaction'.

From forklift side, can we add a step in A1 that says when the scrap bin or hazardous cage is close to full, the operator calls the forklift on the radio instead of dragging bins into the aisle?
That will keep the path clearer.

Yes, that fits well.
I will add a line in A1 under 'housekeeping' that says: 'When scrap or hazardous containers reach the marked fill line, call forklift via radio; do not park extra bins in the aisle'.

The updated steps sound workable.
For the checklist in A2, I suggest we keep it short so people actually use it.
Maybe:
1) Check for obvious hazardous items (batteries, aerosols, paint tins).
2) Check for big sharp metal.
3) Check for liquids in containers if the load looks risky.
4) Confirm PPE is on before starting the load.
We can pilot that on a few shifts for T3.

I like that structure.
Maybe add one more item to A2: 'Walkway and forklift path clear around pilot area before starting the load'.
That ties into the layout work and keeps the compactor corner safer.

Agreed.
So the core items on A2 for every load will be:
1) Look for hazardous items (batteries, aerosols, paint tins, chemicals) and remove them.
2) Remove big sharp metal.
3) If many cans or containers, sample-check for liquids.
4) Confirm PPE is on.
5) Check walkway and forklift path are clear around the pilot area.
We can treat these as the must-do items for T3.
Anything else can be optional notes.

That list is easy to remember.
As long as we have it printed near the infeed, I can follow it on late shift.

Works for me too.
The walkway check will help before we start cleaning.
No extra items from my side.

On the SOP itself (A1), with the updates you listed, I think it covers:
- clear steps from infeed to compactor
- how to handle contaminants and hazardous items
- when to call forklift and how to keep aisles clear.
From my side it is ready to use in the pilot, as long as we keep it to one page front and back so it is readable on the line.

I am ok to use the updated A1 on early shift.
If we see confusion during the pilot, we can tweak wording, but the steps look right.

Same here.
The forklift-related parts in A1 are clear.
Happy to go ahead with this version in the pilot area.

I can follow the steps as written.
No issues from late shift.
Ok to roll with this SOP.

Thanks for the feedback.
I will lock this version of A1 as the standard SOP for the pilot area and final rollout, and freeze the core items on A2 as listed.
If we find issues during the pilot, we will log them and adjust in a later revision, but for now this is our agreed procedure.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on new layout, rotation plan and cleaning routine for the pilot area.

messages.text:
I have sketched a proposed new layout for the pilot area in A6 and a first pass at a rotation and cleaning routine.
This ties into T4, T6 and T12.
Key layout changes:
- move the scrap bin slightly away from the compactor corner to open the forklift path.
- shift the hazardous cage entrance so people do not cross the forklift path.
- mark a clear pedestrian lane along the wall.
For rotation, I drafted a pattern in A8 that mixes heavy picking with lighter tasks.
For cleaning, there is a daily checklist draft similar to what will become A4.
Please review and shout if anything looks unsafe or unworkable on your shift.

Looking at A6, the new forklift path is much cleaner.
Only concern: the turn near the hazardous cage might still be tight if there are pallets waiting.
Could we mark a no-parking zone on the floor there and add that to the cleaning and inspection list in A4 so people keep it clear?

On the rotation in A8, I like that heavy picking is followed by a lighter task.
For early shift, could we make sure no one stays on the compactor area more than one hour at a time?
That spot is noisy and dusty.
We can reflect that in T12.

On the cleaning checklist draft in A4, can we add a step to check under the belt for trapped material at least once per shift?
Right now it builds up and is hard to reach.
Also, we should list which cleaning products to use near the hazardous cage so we do not mix chemicals.

For late shift, the new pedestrian lane in A6 will help.
Sometimes people cut across the forklift path to get to the compactor.
If we put clear tape and signs, that should guide them.
On rotation, I am ok with swapping between picking and baler feeding as shown in A8.

From a recycling and hazardous handling view, moving the hazardous cage entrance away from the main forklift turn is a big improvement.
We just need to keep enough space for the blue drum and other containers inside.
On the cleaning list in A4, I suggest we add a quick visual check that hazardous labels are still readable and containers are closed before we start washing floors nearby.

Good catch.
I will update A6 to mark a no-parking zone at that turn and add a line in A4: 'Check that no pallets or bins are parked in the marked forklift turn area'.
On rotation, I will adjust A8 so no one stays at the compactor more than one hour in a row, as suggested for T12.

On the cleaning steps, I can help detail which products to use where.
For T6, we can say:
- neutral detergent for general floor cleaning.
- no bleach or strong acids near the hazardous cage.
- use absorbent granules for spills.
We can add that to A4 with simple icons.

Yes, that matches what we already use.
If we list it clearly in A4, it will help new staff.
I can test the updated checklist on night shift for T6 and note any issues.

With the no-parking zone and the clearer path in A6, I am comfortable with the new forklift route.
As long as the markings are bright and we keep them in A4 checks, it should stay clear.

I am ok with the new layout too.
The pedestrian lane and no-parking zone will make it easier to see where to walk and where not to leave bins.

From early shift, the updated A6 looks good.
No issues with emergency exits or clearances.
I am fine to confirm this layout for the pilot.

Agree with the others.
The new layout in A6 improves both safety and flow in the pilot area.
I am ok to lock it in and share with the shift supervisor and maintenance for final checks.

Great, we will treat the updated A6 as the agreed layout and forklift paths for the pilot area.
I will send it to the shift supervisor and maintenance for their sign-off under T4.

On the rotation plan in A8, I have now:
- 1 hour at first pick station.
- 1 hour at second pick station.
- 1 hour at compactor area.
- 1 hour on lighter duties (baler feeding, housekeeping, checklist checks).
Then repeat.
This covers a full shift with breaks.
Any concerns with coverage of key positions for T12?

That pattern works for early shift.
We just need to make sure someone is always available to do the A2 load check before starting a new batch.
Maybe we can assign that to whoever is on lighter duties in A8.

For late shift, I am ok with that rotation.
Having a lighter block after compactor duty will help.
No gaps that I can see.

Night shift can follow the same pattern.
During the lighter block we can also do the cleaning checks from A4.
That way the checklist is not forgotten.

Sounds good.
We will use A8 as the standard rotation schedule for the pilot, with the lighter block covering A2 load checks and A4 cleaning checks.
Now on the cleaning routine itself: the updated A4 has tasks split by time of day (start, mid-shift, end) and includes PPE and products.
We also need to agree who signs it off each shift.

I suggest the person on lighter duties at the end of the shift does the final walk-through and signs A4, but the shift supervisor should also initial it when they do their round.
That way it is clear who checked what.

Agree.
Operator signs A4 for the tasks they completed, and the shift supervisor initials once they have verified the area.
This keeps it simple but still accountable.
From my side, the content of A4 now covers what we need for T6.

I am ok with that.
I can sign A4 on night shift and ask the supervisor to initial during their round.

Same for late shift.
Happy to sign the checklist when I am on the lighter block.

Ok, we will lock A4 as the daily cleaning and inspection routine for the pilot area, with the operator on lighter duties signing and the shift supervisor initialling.
I will finalise A6, A8 and A4 and share them for printing so we can start the pilot.

threads.thread_goal: Lock hazardous waste handling rules and incident reporting process.

messages.text:
I have drafted the hazardous waste handling and storage guide for the sorting area (A3) and a quick reference for incident and near-miss reporting (A5).
These are linked to T5, T7 and also touch T9 for collection timing.
The hazardous guide lists common items we see: batteries, aerosols, paint tins, chemicals, electronics, and how to drain, store and label them.
The incident sheet explains when to report, who to call, and how to use the simple card.
Please review and flag anything that does not match what you see on the line.

On A3, the section about draining paint tins says to drain into the red drum.
Can we clarify that only if the label is readable and we know what it is?
Sometimes we get unlabelled containers.
In those cases I think we should not open them on the line.

On A5, the incident examples are clear, but could we add one for a near miss with a forklift in the pilot area?
People see those often but do not always report them.

Agree with adding a forklift near-miss example.
Also, on A3, for batteries, can we say clearly that they go straight into the yellow battery box and never into general scrap?
I still see them mixed in sometimes.

I like the pictures in A3.
One question: for small electronics like phones, do we treat them as hazardous or just as e-waste?
Maybe we can add a simple rule there.

On A5, the steps say to fill in a card and hand it to the supervisor.
Sometimes the supervisor is not on the floor.
Should we also allow dropping the card in a box near the pilot area so it does not get lost?

Good points.
I will update A3 so that:
- only labelled paint or chemical containers are opened and drained into the red drum.
- unlabelled or damaged containers are placed in a sealed over-drum and flagged to the supervisor.
- batteries always go into the yellow battery box, never into scrap.
For small electronics, we can say: 'phones, tablets and similar go into the e-waste crate, not general waste'.

On A5, I will add a forklift near-miss example: 'forklift brakes suddenly to avoid a person or bin in the path, even if no one is hit'.
I will also add a line about the card box near the pilot area so people can drop cards there if the supervisor is not around.
Supervisor will empty the box each shift.

The updated rules in A3 sound safe and practical.
We just need to make sure the over-drum is clearly marked and placed where the forklift can reach it without blocking the path.
We can align that with the layout in A6 and the collection schedule in T9 so it gets emptied regularly.

If we put the over-drum just inside the hazardous cage, I can pick it up with the forklift without blocking the main path.
We should note that in A3 and in the collection timing under T9 so it is cleared at least once a week.

The incident steps in A5 are clear now.
For the pilot area, I suggest we keep it to three simple actions:
1) Make the area safe.
2) Tell the supervisor or call the number on the sheet.
3) Fill in a card and hand it in or drop it in the box.
Anything more and people might skip it.

I like those three steps.
Easy to remember.
We can also use them in the toolbox talk later.

With the pictures and simple rules in A3, I feel more confident about what to do with batteries, aerosols and phones.
No extra questions from me.

So to summarise:
- A3 now lists common hazardous items, where they go, and special rules for labelled vs unlabelled containers.
- A5 has three simple reporting steps plus examples, including forklift near misses.
From my side, A3 is ready to use in the pilot area.
We will still ask the health and safety officer to review it formally, but I am comfortable treating this as our agreed guide.

I agree.
The hazardous guide in A3 is clear enough for all shifts.
We can walk through it quickly during the pilot start.

On the incident process, I am happy to lock the three steps you listed as the standard for the sorting line:
1) Make safe.
2) Tell supervisor or call the number.
3) Fill and hand in or drop a card.
We will put that wording on A5 and use it in T7.

Works for me.
I will start using those three steps on night shift and encourage others to do the same.

Same here.
If we keep A5 posted near the pilot area, it will be easy to follow.
I will also mention it on the radio when we have a near miss.

I will finalise A3 and A5 with these updates and send them to the health and safety officer for formal review.
In parallel, we can start using them in the pilot area so we do not lose time.
I will also check with logistics on T9 to make sure hazardous collections match the new storage setup.

threads.thread_goal: Plan training huddles, PPE needs and go-live date for new routines.

messages.text:
Time to plan how we roll this out.
I have drafted a short toolbox talk script for the new sorting, cleaning and reporting routines, which will become A7 and supports T8.
It covers:
- key changes in A1, A2, A3 and A4.
- the incident steps from A5.
- a quick check of understanding.
We also need to confirm PPE and signage needs for T10 and agree on a go-live date for the pilot and then full line.
Please review the script and share any tweaks or missing points.

The script in A7 reads well.
I suggest we keep it to 15 minutes max and use simple questions like: 'Where do batteries go now?' and 'What are the three steps if you see a spill or near miss?'.
For PPE and signage under T10, we should list:
- gloves, safety glasses, high-vis, safety shoes as standard.
- extra face shields when draining liquids.
- clear signs for the pedestrian lane, no-parking zone, and hazardous cage rules.

On the training content, we should also include a quick demo of how to use A2 and where to find A3 and A5 on the wall.
For new staff, I can later turn this into a short guideline for on-the-job coaching as part of T11.

The script is easy to follow.
I like the idea of asking simple questions.
For PPE, can we make it clear that face shields are only needed when draining or handling liquids, not all the time?
Otherwise people might avoid using them.

For signage, it would help to have:
- a simple map of the pilot area from A6 with arrows for the forklift path and the pedestrian lane.
- icons showing where to find A1, A2, A3, A4 and A5 on the wall.
We can mention that in the toolbox talk so people know where to look.

On PPE, I would add hearing protection for the compactor area.
For signage, a clear 'no pallets here' sign at the forklift turn would help.
We can show that sign during the huddle so people recognise it.

Thanks all.
I will adjust A7 to:
- keep it under 15 minutes.
- include the simple questions you suggested.
- add a quick walk to show where A1–A5 and A4 are posted.
On PPE and signage for T10, I will start a list based on your comments and share it here for final check.

Here is the draft PPE and signage list for T10:
PPE by task:
- General sorting and picking: gloves, safety glasses, high-vis, safety shoes.
- Compactor area: add hearing protection.
- Draining or handling liquids: add face shield and chemical-resistant gloves.
Signage:
- Pedestrian lane and forklift path map from A6.
- No-parking zone at forklift turn.
- Hazardous cage rules and icons for batteries, aerosols, paint, e-waste.
- Poster with the three incident steps from A5.
Anything missing?

Looks complete to me.
Maybe add a small label on the blue drum, red drum and yellow battery box so they match the pictures in A3.
That will help new staff connect the guide to what they see on the floor.

Agree with the list.
If we add the drum labels as suggested, I am happy to treat this as the final PPE and signage set for the pilot and rollout.
We will still ask the health and safety officer to confirm, but we can proceed with ordering and installation.

From my side, that covers what we need.
The no-parking sign and floor markings will make a big difference.

I am ok with that PPE list.
Clear enough to remember.
No extra items from me.

Same here.
The incident poster from A5 will help remind people about the three steps.

Ok, I will finalise the PPE and signage list for T10 with the drum labels and send it to the health and safety officer for confirmation.
Now we need to agree on timing.
Given where we are, I propose:
- Run toolbox talks using A7 on all shifts over the next three days.
- Start the pilot area go-live with new SOP, layout, cleaning and incident process next Monday.
- If no major issues, extend to the full line one week after that.
Does that work for everyone?

That schedule works for early shift.
Three days is enough to cover everyone with A7.
Starting the pilot next Monday gives us time to get markings and signs in place.

I am aligned with that plan.
I can help run the toolbox talks and answer questions about A1–A5.
If we see any big issues in the first week of the pilot, we can adjust before rolling to the full line.

Works for me.
I will make sure forklift drivers on all shifts attend one of the huddles before the pilot starts.

Late shift can do the huddle at the start of the shift.
The Monday pilot start is fine.

Night shift is ok with that timing too.
We can do the toolbox talk just before we start the main loads.

Great, then we will lock in:
- Toolbox talks with A7 on all shifts over the next three days.
- Pilot go-live next Monday in the agreed pilot area.
- Full line rollout one week later if the pilot goes well.
I will update A7 with the final script and coordinate with the shift supervisors.
